info.title: boxbox
info.description: the boxbox server: a password gate, the hosts it watches, the fleet as one stream with a cursor, transcripts read through it, the verbs a person answers asks and starts turns with (each with a clientID), the rest of a session's write path (queue, steer, commands, shells, unsend), terminals relayed through it, push and presence, needs and read state, and the telemetry ingest. every route but login and logout needs the session cookie.

post.summary:
clears threads off home on every device. a thread comes back on its own
when it works again, asks, or is updated; it stays in history.

200.description: which threads left home and which could not

get.summary: the fleet model now.

200.description: every host, session and ask, and the window order

get.summary:
a page of history: every machine's threads older than the cursor, newest
first, with the cleared ones marked.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: matches a thread's title or its repo, any case.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: the cursor a page answered with (`next`): threads after it, newest first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: threads in the page, 1 to 100; 30 when absent.

200.description: a page, and the cursor for the next

400.description: a search or limit out of range

get.summary: each host, configured ones in `boxbox.toml` order, then paired ones.

post.summary:
trades a one-time token for the host's bearer credential, keeps it
server-side and starts watching the host.

201.description: paired; the host is being watched

400.description: the address, token or name is not usable

409.description: the name or the address is already here

422.description: the daemon refused the token, or does not pair

delete.summary:
forgets a paired host: its credential is deleted and its watcher stops.
the daemon keeps its record until `cmx2 pair --revoke boxbox` there.

409.description: the host is set in boxbox.toml

get.summary: the `/` commands the thread's directory offers.

parameters.name: directory
parameters.description: the session's directory on the host.

get.summary: files in a project matching what was typed after `@`, relative paths.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: at most this many, 1 to 200; the daemon's default is 10.

get.summary: the folders inside a folder on the host, so a thread can start in a place no thread has been in yet.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: absolute, `~` or `~/...`; the host's home when left out.

parameters.name: hidden
parameters.description: also list the folders whose names start with a dot.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description:
only the folders whose names start with this, case aside: the server narrows a big folder
before it answers, so a typed word never pulls the whole list to a phone.

400.description: nothing at that path on the host, a file, or not readable

get.summary: the models a host can run, for the per-repo defaults.

502.description: the host did not answer, refused the credential or failed

post.summary:
answers a permission. an ask already settled is 409 with who settled it
and when; an ask the daemon does not know is 404.

404.description: no such host, or the ask is gone

409.description: already settled; `error.settled` says by whom and when

get.summary: the repos a new thread can start in, newest activity first.

the host's providers and models, and its defaults, for the composer's
model and effort row.

parameters.name: directory
parameters.description: the project directory the list is for.

get.summary:
the host's open terminals: running ones, and exited ones a session
started (cmx2 drops a person's once it exits).

502.description: the host did not answer or refused the credential

post.summary: opens a terminal on the host, as a person's (it goes when it exits).

400.description: not a new terminal, or the directory does not exist

502.description: the host did not answer or refused the credential

get.summary: the login shells the host lists, the host user's own first.

200.description: cmx2's `{path, name, acceptable}` list, byte for byte

502.description: the host did not answer or refused the credential

get.summary: one terminal.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: the terminal's id on the host

502.description: the host did not answer or refused the credential

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: the terminal's id on the host

200.description: the terminal after the change, cmx2's `PtyInfo`

400.description: not a change, or a size out of range

502.description: the host did not answer or refused the credential

delete.summary: kills a terminal and has the host forget it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: the terminal's id on the host

502.description: the host did not answer or refused the credential

get.summary:
the terminal's bytes, as a websocket: cmx2's pty stream relayed, plus
the relay's replay and heartbeat frames (docs/terminal.md).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: the terminal's id on the host

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
resume from here, in utf-16 units: the cursor of the last output
applied. `-1` is from now on; absent replays everything retained.

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: the pane's device id, for the relay's telemetry rows.

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: the pane's device class, for the same.

101.description: the websocket; every later outcome is a close code (docs/terminal.md)

400.description: not a websocket request, or a cursor below -1

403.description: the page asking is not boxbox's

post.summary: answers a question.

404.description: no such host, or the ask is gone

409.description: already settled; `error.settled` says by whom and when

post.summary: dismisses a question without an answer.

404.description: no such host, or the ask is gone

post.summary:
the daemon re-reads its config and flushes skills, agents, commands,
the model list and language servers, and reconnects mcp servers.
sessions are untouched.

502.description: the host did not answer, refused the credential or failed

get.summary: a repo's favicon from its host, or 404 when there is none to show.

parameters.name: root
parameters.description: the repo's project root on the host, absolute. a worktree's directory finds no icon: ask for the root.

200.description: the image, with its content type found from its bytes; `cache-control: private, max-age=21600` and an `etag`

400.description: root is not an absolute path, or is `/`

404.description: no icon to show, with no body (an unknown host answers the usual json error instead). `x-repo-icon` says why (none, unproven, unsupported, refused, retry) and `cache-control` how long to believe it: 30 minutes when the repo was searched, 60 seconds for a root the host has not shown to be real, 5 minutes when the host cannot read files yet, an hour for the host user's home or a directory above it (never listed), `no-store` when the search could not finish

post.summary:
the daemon aborts every running turn, closes its streams and exits for
its supervisor to start a fresh one. the host's watcher sees the stream
end and reconnects to the new daemon from its cursor.

502.description: the host did not answer, refused the credential or failed

post.summary:
starts a thread in a repo with its first message: a fresh worktree first when asked, then the
session, then the prompt, armed for "done". a retry with the same client id answers the thread
the first try made.

200.description: a retry: the thread the first try made

400.description: not a thread, or no folder there on the host

502.description: the host did not answer, or refused the worktree

post.summary:
stops the running turn. a fault that follows within 15 s is the
person's own action, never pushed.

reads a thread from its daemon and lets the fleet adopt it, for a thread
opened from history that the fleet does not hold. the fleet's stream
then carries its entry like any session's.

204.description: the fleet holds the thread now

404.description: no such host or thread, or it was archived

post.summary:
archives a thread through its daemon: it leaves every listing and its
history stays on disk. a turn that is running is stopped first, by the
daemon.

422.description: the daemon refused, with its own words (`host-said`)

502.description: the host did not answer or failed

post.summary:
runs a `/` command as a prompt. the daemon holds its answer until the command's turn settles, so
this answers 202 once the daemon has taken it and leaves the rest to the stream (the echo of the
client id), keeping the request alive in the background so the daemon is never cut off mid-turn.

202.description: taken; the stream carries the rest

404.description: no such host, session, or command

post.summary:
compacts the thread now, on the model it already uses. the daemon answers once the summary is in, so a thread with
a turn running is refused (stop it first), and a failed compaction leaves the thread as it was.

200.description: compacted; the summary is in the thread

422.description: the daemon refused: a turn is running, or the thread is imported history

502.description: the host did not answer within five minutes, or the compaction failed and the thread is unchanged

post.summary: runs what is queued now, on an idle session ("run now" after a stop).

get.summary:
the session's messages, as cmx2's `GET /session/{session}/message`
answers them, the one still streaming included (cmx2-asks a5).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: at most this many messages, newest last; all of them when absent.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: the `x-next-cursor` of the page after this one.

200.description: cmx2's message list, byte for byte, with `x-cmx2-seq`

404.description: no such host, or the daemon has no such session

get.summary:
one message of the session, `{info, parts}`, streaming or finished; a
client re-reads a part through this when a delta shows it missed text.

200.description: cmx2's `{info, parts}`, byte for byte, with `x-cmx2-seq`

404.description: no such host, session or message

delete.summary: takes back a queued prompt before the model sees it ("unsend").

404.description: no such host, session or queued message

post.summary:
sends a prompt (it starts a turn, or queues behind the running one) and
arms that turn: when it is done, the device's person hears of it.
a prompt for after the running turn; on an idle session it starts one.

202.description: accepted: cmx2's answer, byte for byte, with `messageID`

409.description: the daemon refused it: cmx2's `{name, data}`

get.summary:
what the branch of a session's checkout holds beyond its base: commits,
files with line counts, the patch, and whether it merges clean.

200.description: cmx2's diff of the checkout, byte for byte, with `checkout`

404.description: no such host, session or checkout

422.description: the daemon refused, with its own words (`host-said`)

502.description: the host did not answer or failed

post.summary:
removes the session's checkout and its branch without merging. when it
held work, its last state is kept first under a ref the answer names.

200.description: discarded: cmx2's answer, byte for byte

404.description: no such host, session or checkout

409.description: a turn is running in the checkout: `busy`

422.description: the daemon refused, with its own words (`host-said`)

502.description: the host did not answer or failed

post.summary:
squash-merges the session's checkout into its base on its machine, then
removes the checkout and its branch. nothing is pushed.

200.description: merged: cmx2's answer, byte for byte

404.description: no such host, session or checkout

409.description: the daemon would not merge it: `busy`, `conflict` (with `files`) or `refused` (with `reason`)

422.description: the daemon refused, with its own words (`host-said`)

502.description: the host did not answer or failed

post.summary:
runs a `!` line in the thread's directory. it starts no turn; the agent reads the output on its
next one. the daemon answers when the line has finished, with the shell message.

steers text into the running turn: the agent reads it at its next step. on an idle thread it
starts a turn, which is then armed for "done" like any prompt.
exchanges the password for the session cookie.

200.description: signed in; the session cookie is set

400.description: the body is not a login

401.description: wrong password, answered after the flat delay

post.summary: clears the session cookie.

200.description: signed out; the session cookie is cleared

post.summary: stores one file: the raw bytes of an image, audio, video or document.

requestBody.description: the file's raw bytes, at most 64 MiB. `content-type` is its type (`application/octet-stream` when absent); `x-boxbox-filename` its name, percent-encoded; for a voice note, `x-boxbox-duration-ms` and `x-boxbox-waveform` (base64 of at most 64 bytes)

201.description: stored, or already held (the same answer for the same bytes)

400.description: a header boxbox cannot read, an empty body, or a body that stopped arriving

413.description: past 64 MiB, refused as the announced length or the bytes pass it

415.description: a declared image, audio or video type the bytes contradict, in words

503.description: `media-busy`: four uploads are running (with `retry-after`); or the store is not answering

507.description: `media-full`: nothing old enough to evict makes room; raise `[media] max_bytes`

get.summary: a stored file, whole or one range of it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: the media id: the sha256 of the bytes, 64 lowercase hex

200.description: the whole file (also for several ranges), with `accept-ranges: bytes`, `cache-control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable`, `etag: "<id>"`, the stored `content-type` for image, audio, video and pdf (`application/octet-stream` for every other kind) and a `content-disposition` (inline for image, audio, video and pdf; attachment otherwise)

410.description: `media-evicted`: the store made room for newer files

416.description: the range starts past the end, with `content-range: bytes */<size>`

get.summary:
the open needs and the ones served lately, with `x-boxbox-seq`: the
journal position they reflect, so a stream resumed from it carries
every later move and nothing twice.

every preference: each device's appearance, each repo's defaults, the
favourite models.

put.summary: sets one device's theme and motion.

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: the device id the app minted

put.summary:
sets the favourite models, in order. repeats are dropped, keeping the
first; the answer is the list as saved.

400.description: an id is empty, too long or has control characters, or there are more than 64

put.summary:
sets the model and effort a new thread in one repo starts with; with
neither, the daemon's defaults apply again.

400.description: the host is unknown, or a value is not usable

post.summary:
what this device is showing; sent on every change and every 30 s while
the app is visible and focused.

get.summary: the push key and every subscribed device.

200.description: the vapid key and the subscribed devices

post.summary: saves this device's subscription (replacing any it had).

400.description: not a subscription boxbox can push to; the message says which part

post.summary:
pushes a test notice to one device, through the same decision, rate
and dedupe as every other.

202.description: queued; `push.decided` says what became of it

400.description: not a test the server can send

post.summary: forgets this device's subscription.

200.description: the device is no longer pushed

post.summary:
marks a session seen by one device, through the message it shows. the
mark never moves back, and the session's mark is the furthest of its
devices' (`design.md`, unread from here).

404.description: no such session in the fleet

get.summary: the fleet, live.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
the cursor, `<epoch>:<seq>`, for clients that cannot set
`Last-Event-ID`; the header wins when both are sent.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: the id of the last frame applied, `<epoch>:<seq>`

200.description: an sse stream: `hello`, then a replay or a `reset`, then live entries; each frame's data is one of these
normalized and queued for the day file

503.description: the writer is backed up; send again

dropped.description: events dropped whole (unknown kind, or a kind the server owns).

Archived.description: the daemon's answer to an archive.

archived.description: when the daemon archived it, ms since the epoch on its clock.

Ask.description: a permission or a question waiting on a person.

request.description: cmx2's `PermissionRequest` or `QuestionRequest`, as the daemon wrote it.

directory.description: where it runs: the checkout, or the fresh worktree.

repeat.description: true when this answers a retry of a birth already made.

session.description: the new session's id; with the host it is the thread's key.

oneOf.description:
a boxbox device, by its id, with the class it named itself by
("iphone", "mac") so a surface can say where.
a person, through a client that is not boxbox; the daemon's `by`.
nobody: the agent or the daemon.

By.description:
who served a need: a person on one of their devices, a person somewhere
boxbox cannot name (another client of the daemon), or nobody (the agent
moved on, the daemon dropped it).

oneOf.description: a host's connection or health changed.
a host left `boxbox.toml`; everything the fleet held for it goes.

the host was read afresh (a cold connect, or the daemon's
`stream.reset`): these replace every session and ask the fleet held
for it. a client re-reads any open transcript on this host.
a session appeared or changed: the whole entry, replacing the last.
a permission or question now waits on a person.
an ask was answered, rejected, or dropped with its turn.
the window order changed: every key, first first.
a message was created or changed (cmx2 `message.updated`).

info.description: cmx2's `MessageInfo`, as the daemon wrote it.

upstream.description:
the daemon's seq for this event; apply it only past the seq of
the transcript read it lands on. null when the daemon did not
log it, which makes it newer than any read.

oneOf.description: a part was created or replaced whole (cmx2 `message.part.updated`).

part.description: cmx2's `Part`, as the daemon wrote it.

upstream.description:
null on the daemon's resume re-send of a part still streaming,
which carries its full text so far and no seq.

oneOf.description:
streamed text for a part (cmx2 `message.part.delta`, never logged
by the daemon, so it has no seq).

offset.description:
utf-16 units of the part's text before this delta: a client
appends only when it equals what it holds, skips what it
already has, and re-reads the part on a gap.

Change.description: a change to the fleet model, discriminated on `type`.

CheckoutRefusal.description: why the daemon would not merge or discard a checkout, as the review card reads it.

error.description:
`busy` (a turn runs in the checkout), `conflict` (the branch conflicts with its
base) or `refused` (see `reason`).

ClearBody.description: threads to clear off home, and from which control.

ClearSource.description: which control cleared them, for telemetry.

Cleared.description: how a clear went: the threads now off home, and the ones that could not be.

CommandChoice.description: a `/` command a menu can offer.

hints.description: `$1`, `$ARGUMENTS`: what it takes after its name.

oneOf.description: the first frame of every connection; it carries no id.

build.description: the server's build; a newer one lights "update ready".

epoch.description: the journal this server holds; a restart mints a new one.

oneOf.description:
the client's cursor cannot be replayed: this snapshot replaces
everything it holds, and live entries follow from `seq`.

Control.description: the stream's frames that are not journal entries.

Document.description: a file on a message that is not a photo: a document the host reads to the model.

filename.description: the file's name as the person had it; the host labels the file with it.

url.description:
`data:<mime>;base64,...`: a pdf of at most 9 mb, a text or json file of at most 512 kb; with the
photos, at most 18 mb of files on one message.

answer.description: the daemon's answer, as it wrote it.

repeat.description:
true when the daemon had already acted on this `clientID` and
repeated its first answer.

ErrorBody.description: the body of every error answer.

code.description:
stable, for code: `sign-in`, `wrong-password`, `bad-request`,
`batch-too-large`, `busy`, `store-down`, `not-found`, `app-missing`,
`vite-down`, `unknown-host`, `host-taken`, `address-taken`,
`configured-host`, `pair-refused`, `pair-unsupported`,
`pair-unreachable`, `pair-failed`, `host-failed`,
`credential-revoked`, `host-unreachable`, `host-refused`,
`no-such-terminal`, `foreign-origin`, `stopping`, `no-such-session`,
`gone`, `settled`, `already-sent`, `host-said`, `no-such-checkout`,
`checkout-refused` (whose body is a `CheckoutRefusal`, not this one),
and contract 2's `no-such-agent`, `agent-unreachable`, `agent-busy`
(with `retry-after`), `generation-changed`, `not-confirmed`,
`not-built`, `attachment-too-large`, `attachment-kind`, `name-reserved`.

message.description: for people, in the interface's voice.

oneOf.description: on `settled`: who answered first, and when.

FleetSnapshot.description: the whole fleet model, as `reset` and `GET /api/fleet` carry it.

order.description: the window order: session keys, first first.

Folder.description: a folder on the host, for the new-thread sheet's picker.

directory.description: its absolute path on the host.

repo.description: it holds a `.git`, so a fresh worktree can be made from it.

Folders.description: the folders inside one folder on a host.

children.description: the folders inside it that start with the prefix asked, visible first, then by name; at most 500.

home.description: the host user's home, where a walk starts.

parent.description: the folder above it; none at the root.

path.description: the folder read, absolute and resolved.

truncated.description: more folders matched than `children` holds: type more of the name to narrow it.

FrameCounts.description: frames read from the host since the server started.

duplicates.description:
events a resume replayed at or below the cursor, dropped so none
applies twice.

undecodable.description:
frames that did not decode into the generated `Event` union, or were
over the frame cap; each was logged and skipped.

checkedAt.description: when this answer arrived, ms since the epoch.

contract.description: the contract version the daemon speaks.

contractMatches.description: whether that is the contract boxbox's types were generated from.

next.description:
where the next page starts (`before`); absent at the end. opaque: send
it back as it came. a page can be empty with a cursor: a search that
matched nothing yet.

unreached.description: machines left out of this page.

HistoryRow.description:
one thread of history. its status, asks and tail are the fleet's, for a
thread the fleet holds; the rest is the daemon's listing.

cleared.description: the thread is cleared off home now.

info.description: cmx2's `SessionInfo`, as the daemon wrote it.

HostMemory.description: what the daemon says about its own memory.

liveSessions.description: sessions the daemon holds in memory; none means it is idle.

sampledAt.description: when the sample was taken, ms since the epoch.

default.description: `<provider>/<model>` the daemon starts a thread with, when it says.

HostOrigin.description: where a host came from, which decides who may change it.

connects.description: connections made since the server started.

cursor.description:
the watcher's cursor, `<epoch>:<seq>`, as of the last connection
change: where that connection resumed from, or where the one before
it stopped. null before the host was first read.

oneOf.description:
the last `/global/health` answer; kept while the host is down so the
ui can say which version was last seen.

lastError.description: why the last connection ended or failed, in plain words.

oneOf.description:
the daemon's own memory report, sampled while connected; null until
the first sample, and for a daemon that does not report it.

name.description: the host's name, from `boxbox.toml` or given when it was paired.

reportsSystem.description:
whether the daemon answers `GET /global/system`: false for an older
cmx2, absent until it was first asked.

since.description: when `connection` last changed, ms since the epoch.

oneOf.description:
what the host is and how it is doing (`GET /global/system`), sampled
every 30 s while connected and kept while it is away; absent until the
first sample, and for a daemon without the route.

HostSystem.description:
one sample of the host's system, as the daemon said it, with the time
boxbox read it.

at.description: when the daemon took the sample, ms since the epoch, in its clock.

oneOf.description:
the disk holding the daemon's data; none when the daemon could not
read it.

sampledAt.description: when boxbox read it, ms since the epoch, in the server's clock.

uptime.description: how long the host has been up, in seconds.

load.description: the load averages over 1, 5 and 15 minutes.

rss.description: the daemon's resident set size, in bytes.

uptime.description: how long the daemon has been up, in seconds.

available.description: bytes free for the daemon's user.

path.description: the mount the numbers are for.

model.description: what the hardware says it is: `Mac mini`, `Google Compute Engine`.

virtual.description: whether the host is a virtual machine.

available.description: bytes a new process could have without the host swapping.

name.description: the os as a person names it: `macOS`, `Ubuntu`, `Debian`.

How.description: how a need was served. the names are telemetry values.

seq.description: contiguous within an epoch; the entry's sse id is `<epoch>:<seq>`.

JournalEntry.description:
one journal entry: a change to the fleet model, at its place in the
journal.

MediaObject.description: one stored file, as the upload answers it and parts carry it.

id.description: the sha256 of the bytes, 64 lowercase hex.

waveform.description: at most 64 values from 0 to 255, the loudness of equal slices.

message.description: made from the branch's commits when absent or blank.

efforts.description: the model's variants: its efforts, then the profile's named ones.

ModelPrefs.description: the models a person keeps at the top of every picker, on every device.

favorites.description:
`<provider>/<model>` ids, in the order the person put them. an id no
host lists any more stays until they unpin it.

ModelRef.description: a model, as cmx2 names one.

ask.description: the ask's id, on a permission or a question.

body.description:
the question, the command it wants to run, the result line, the
reason; at most 240 characters.

checkout.description: the checkout's name, on a review.

id.description:
stable per event: `ask:<host>:<ask id>`, `done:<key>:<message id>`,
`fault:<key>:<message id or seq>`, `review:<key>:<checkout>:<event seq or t<ms>>` (one per request),
`job:<key>:<process id>:<reason>`. the push notice for it carries
the same id.

raisedAt.description: when boxbox raised it, ms since the epoch on the server's clock.

rank.description: its place in the inbox: 0 wants you, 1 failed, 2 done or news.

servedAt.description: when it was served; absent while open.

title.description: "ledger wants you", "api is done", in the voice.

NeedKind.description:
what a need is about. the names are the telemetry `need` values and
never change.

NeedsList.description: what waits on the person, and what was served lately.

open.description:
open needs in inbox order: wants you (oldest first), failed, then
done and news (newest first).

served.description: needs served lately, newest first, with who served them and when.

NewTerminal.description: a new terminal. with no command it is the host's login shell.

command.description:
a program to run instead of the login shell, such as another
shell's path from `/shells`.

cwd.description: where it starts; the host's home when absent.

NewThread.description: a new thread in a repo, with its first message.

directory.description: the repo's directory on the host.

NotCleared.description: a thread that stayed on home, and why, in words a window can show.

Pair.description: what `cmx2 pair` printed, and what to call the machine.

name.description: lowercase letters, digits and dashes; from the address when absent.

clientID.description: a uuid the device picks once per answer and reuses on a retry.

message.description: with reject: what the agent should do instead.

mime.description:
`image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/webp`, `image/gif`, or `image/heic` or `image/heif` (the
original of a photo the browser could not decode; the host converts it to jpeg).

url.description:
`data:<mime>;base64,...`: at most 1.5 mb, or for heic and heif a file of at most 9 mb; the photos of
one message at most 18 mb of files together.

PresenceReport.description: `POST /api/presence`: what one device is showing right now.

device.description: the device id the app minted once for this browser profile.

focused.description: `document.hasFocus()`: boxbox is the app in front, not behind another.

thread.description: the thread on stage, `host:session`, or null on home.

windowsInView.description: threads whose windows are in view, `host:session` each.

ProjectChoice.description: a repo a new thread can start in, newest activity first.

directory.description: the repo's main checkout on the host.

updated.description: last activity, ms since the epoch.

Prompt.description: a prompt from a device; the turn it starts is armed for "done".

effort.description:
one of the model's efforts; cmx2 makes it the thread's effort from
this message on.

files.description: files that are not photos (a pdf, text, json), as their own bytes in `data:` urls.

model.description:
`provider/model`, from `/api/hosts/{host}/models`; cmx2 makes it the
thread's model from this message on.

photos.description: photos, resized on the device, as `data:` urls.

kinds.description: the kinds this device is pushed.

since.description: when it first subscribed, ms since the epoch.

PushKind.description:
the kinds a person turns on per device (`design.md`, attention: "which
of the four kinds push. that is the whole settings page for push").

publicKey.description:
the vapid public key, base64url: pass it to `pushManager.subscribe`
as `applicationServerKey`.

PushTest.description:
a test notice to one device: the kind picks the shape (an ask carries
answer and open), and a real thread and ask make the links land.

ask.description: the ask to focus, for kind ask.

QuestionAnswer.description:
an answer to a question: one list of chosen labels (or typed text) per
question it asked.

ReadBody.description: a device has seen a session through one message.

at.description: that message's `time.created`, as the daemon wrote it (ms).

message.description: the newest message the device has in front of it.

ReadMark.description:
a session's read mark as every surface gets it: the furthest any
device has seen.

at.description:
the daemon's `time.created` of the newest message seen, ms: a
message created after it is unread.

markedAt.description: when it was marked, ms since the epoch on the server's clock.

changed.description: config files that changed since the daemon last read them.

flushed.description: what the daemon flushed: skills, agents, commands, models.

RepoPrefs.description:
what a new thread in one repo starts with. absent means the daemon's
own default.

directory.description: the repo's directory on that host, as cmx2 names it.

effort.description: one of the model's variants: an effort, or a named variant.

Send.description:
a prompt, a queued prompt or a steer: what the person typed, with what
they attached and the model and effort they chose for it.

agent.description: an agent to address, by name.

clientID.description:
a uuid the client picks and keeps for a retry, so a flaky network
cannot double a prompt (cmx2-asks a4).

effort.description: the effort for this message: low, medium, high, xhigh or max.

oneOf.description: the model for this message; the session's default when absent.

parts.description: attachments: a photo or document as a data url, or an `@` mention as a file url.

url.description: a `data:` url for a photo or document, a `file://` url for a mention.

SessionEntry.description:
one session in the fleet, identity `host:session` (repos never merge
across hosts).

agents.description: child sessions with a turn running now.

cleared.description:
set while the person has this thread cleared off home: the session's
`time.updated` when they cleared it. absent otherwise, and the moment
the thread does something new (`clears.rs`).

info.description: cmx2's `SessionInfo`, as the daemon wrote it.

needs.description: what waits on a person here, most pressing first (`needs.rs`).

processes.description: background jobs a parked session waits on.

oneOf.description:
how far the person has seen, on the daemon's clock; null before
any device has looked (`read.rs`).

status.description: cmx2's `SessionStatus`; null when idle and not parked.

tail.description: the window's tail: the last parts, oldest first, at most 12.

SettledBy.description: who settled an ask first, as the daemon says (cmx2 a6).

at.description: when, ms since the epoch; null when the daemon did not say.

by.description: the device class or client that answered ("iphone", "mac").

SlashCommand.description: a `/` command and what was typed after its name.

Steer.description: text with photos and files, steered into the running turn.

StreamFrame.description:
one frame's data on `GET /api/stream`: a control frame or a journal
entry, discriminated on `type` across both.

Subscribe.description: a `PushSubscription` as `toJSON()` gives it, plus who it belongs to.

deviceClass.description: one of the telemetry dictionary's device classes.

kinds.description: the kinds to push; all four when absent.

TailItem.description:
one part as a window shows it, reduced to what the window needs. parts
a window does not show (step markers, snapshots, the context the daemon
adds to a prompt, a prompt still queued) never enter a tail. streamed
text grows the part as it arrives (`message.part.delta`).

from.description:
the agent that sent the part, when it is another agent's report or
note (cmx2's mail envelope): the window says who, not "you".

role.description: who wrote the part's message: your prompt sits on the right.

text.description:
at most 280 characters: the end of the agent's text, the start of
your prompt, or the tool's title.

tool.description: the tool's name, on tool parts.

TailRole.description: cmx2's message roles, as the daemon names them.

TelemetryBatch.description:
the body is read whatever its content type says, because
`navigator.sendBeacon` posts `text/plain`.

device.description: the producer's device id, minted once per browser profile or board.

deviceClass.description: one of the dictionary's device classes, claimed explicitly.

events.description: raw events: `{kind, id?, at?, surface?, host?, session?, repo?, ok?, ms?, props?}`.

TerminalChange.description: a rename, a resize, or both.

id.description:
the notice id, the join key in `push.decided`, `push.sent` and
`push.delivered`.

Unreached.description: a machine that did not answer, and why.

removed.description: false when the device had no subscription.

Verb.description: dismissing a question, or stopping a turn.

WorktreeDiscarded.description: cmx2's answer to a discard, as it came.

snapshot.description: the commit that keeps the checkout's last state, when it held work.

stopped.description: processes stopped because they ran in the checkout.

WorktreeMerged.description: cmx2's answer to a merge, as it came.

into.description: where the base is checked out; the merge ran there.

stopped.description: processes stopped because they ran in the checkout.

WorktreeReview.description:
what a checkout's branch holds beyond its base: cmx2's answer as it came,
with `checkout` added.

checkout.description: the checkout's name when the session has an open review need, else null.

commits.description: commits on the branch beyond its base.

diff.description: the unified patch of the commits, 2 MB at most.

dirty.description: uncommitted changes in the checkout: merge refuses until they are committed.

mergeable.description: false when the branch conflicts with its base; absent when the daemon did not say.
